items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: the main attraction was a lesbian named Gladys Lentley. Gladys was quite plump and wore a man's full dress suit for her act...

ctx.x: During the months that Teddy was at the Savoy, an orchestra by the name of the Alabama State College was engaged for a few days. The leader was named Erskine Hawkins and he was the second trumpet player I ever heard that could play altissimo C or C above the high one in the treble clef. The first one was with Jimmie Lunceford whom I heard at the Lafayette shortly after I came back from Europe.

After a few months at the Savoy, Teddy Hill and orchestra were engaged to play at the Ubangi Club which had been Connie's Inn and Harlem Club before. In place of having girls in the line up, there were six female impersonators and the main attraction was a lesbian named Gladys Lentley. Gladys was quite plump and wore a man's full dress suit for her act and dressed like a man except for a skirt when she had on street clothes. Gladys played piano, sang and tap danced a little.

Allen Drew was a cigar-smoking manager of ceremonies and comedian. A girl pianist and singer by the name of Una Mae Carlisle was also engaged at the club and she was a protege of Fats Waller when he was playing for the WLLW. radio station in Cincinnati.
